content: Lansoprazole is a medication used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, and erosive esophagitis. It is also used to treat infections caused by Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) and other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Mechanism of Action: Lansoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced by the stomach. It achieves this by inhibiting the proton pumps in the stomach lining, which are responsible for acid secretion. Dosage Forms: Lansoprazole is available under the brand names Prevacid, Prevacid 24HR, and as generic lansoprazole. It comes in the following oral dosage forms: 15 mg delayed-release capsules 30 mg delayed-release capsules 15 mg delayed-release orally disintegrating tablets 30 mg delayed-release orally disintegrating tablets Storage Instructions: Lansoprazole should be stored at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. How to Use: Lansoprazole capsules should be swallowed whole. Orally disintegrating tablets dissolve in the mouth. If you have difficulty swallowing capsules, you may open them and sprinkle the contents on a tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without chewing. Take lansoprazole before meals. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects include: Diarrhea Stomach pain Nausea Constipation If these side effects persist or bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Other side effects may occur, so contact your provider if you suspect any adverse reactions. Serious Side Effects: 1. Kidney Problems: Acute interstitial nephritis can occur at any time during treatment. Symptoms include reduced urine output or blood in the urine. Contact your doctor immediately if these occur. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can cause severe diarrhea. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, and fever. Seek medical attention if these symptoms develop. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Rare but serious conditions like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) can occur. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes, blisters, and watery eyes. Stop the medication and seek emergency care if these symptoms appear. 4. DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms): This multi-organ hypersensitivity reaction can affect the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop the medication and seek immediate medical help if these occur. 5. Lupus: Lansoprazole can trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune condition. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain and rashes on the arms or cheeks. Inform your provider if these symptoms develop. 6. Vitamin B12 Deficiency: Long-term use (3 years or more) can reduce vitamin B12 absorption, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling in the hands or feet. Contact your provider if these occur. 7. Hypomagnesemia: Prolonged use can cause low magnesium levels, which may result in seizures, muscle spasms, dizziness, or heart rhythm problems. Inform your provider if you experience these symptoms. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term or high-dose use, especially in older adults, may increase the risk of bone fractures. 9. Severe Allergic Reactions: Symptoms include difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, hives, dizziness, or nausea. Stop the medication and seek emergency care if these occur. Precautions: Do not use lansoprazole if you are allergic to it, other proton pump inhibitors, or any of its ingredients. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as lansoprazole may interact with other drugs. Do not take lansoprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and instructions. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Lansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. Special Populations: Pregnancy: The effects of lansoprazole on pregnancy are not well understood. Inform your provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Lansoprazole can pass into breast milk. Do not use it while breastfeeding. Children under 1 year: Use in infants may carry additional risks. Discuss with your provider. Drug Interactions: Lansoprazole may interact with certain medications, including: Methotrexate Digoxin Warfarin Theophylline Clarithromycin Tacrolimus Antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir) St. John’s Wort Rifampin Always inform your provider about all medications and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much lansoprazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double doses. Uses: Lansoprazole is used to treat: Heartburn GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) Ulcers Erosive esophagitis Excessive stomach acid production H. pylori infections It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider.
